Algorithms & Implementation
============================

.. contents:: On this page
   :depth: 3
   :local:

This page describes the numerical algorithms used in **hftest**,
covering: Boys function evaluation, the McMurchie-Davidson integral
engine, direct SCF with Schwarz screening, and Pulay DIIS.

Boys Function
--------------

The *Boys function* of order :math:`n` appears as the fundamental
building block of all nuclear-attraction and electron-repulsion
integrals over Gaussian basis functions:

.. math::
   :label: boys

   F_n(x) = \int_0^1 t^{2n}\, e^{-x t^2}\, dt
           = \frac{1}{2}\, x^{-(n+\tfrac{1}{2})}\,
             \gamma\!\left(n+\tfrac{1}{2},\, x\right),

where :math:`\gamma` is the lower incomplete Gamma function.

Regime 1 — Trivial limit (:math:`x \le 10^{-14}`)
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

When :math:`x \approx 0` the integrand equals :math:`t^{2n}` and

.. math::

   F_n(0) = \frac{1}{2n+1}.

Regime 2 — Taylor series (:math:`0 < x < 1`)
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

For small positive :math:`x` the exponential is expanded:

.. math::

   F_n(x) = \int_0^1 t^{2n}\sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{(-x)^k t^{2k}}{k!}\,dt
           = \sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{(-x)^k}{k!\,(2n+2k+1)}.

The partial-sum loop breaks when the absolute term drops below
:math:`10^{-16}` (typically converges in fewer than 30 terms for
:math:`x < 1`).

Regime 3 — Analytic :math:`F_0` + upward recurrence (:math:`x \ge 1`)
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

For large :math:`x` the :math:`n = 0` case has the closed form

.. math::

   F_0(x) = \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2\sqrt{x}}\,\operatorname{erf}(\sqrt{x}).

Higher orders are then generated by the **upward recurrence**:

.. math::
   :label: upward

   F_{n+1}(x) = \frac{(2n+1)\,F_n(x) - e^{-x}}{2x}.

For very large :math:`x`, cancellation in :eq:`upward` can make the
result non-finite.  In that case the **asymptotic approximation** is
used as a fallback:

.. math::

   F_n(x) \approx \frac{(2n-1)!!\,\sqrt{\pi}}{2^{n+1}\, x^{n+\tfrac{1}{2}}}
   \quad (x \to \infty).

The function ``boys_Fvec(nmax, x, F[])`` computes all orders
:math:`F_0, F_1, \ldots, F_{n_\text{max}}` in a single pass, which is
critical for performance in the integral engine.

McMurchie-Davidson Integral Engine
------------------------------------

All one- and two-electron integrals are computed using the
**McMurchie-Davidson** (MD) scheme [MD1978]_.  The key idea is to
expand a product of two Cartesian Gaussians

.. math::

   G_{ij}(r,\alpha,\beta,X_{AB})
   = (r-A)^i\,e^{-\alpha(r-A)^2}\cdot(r-B)^j\,e^{-\beta(r-B)^2}

as a linear combination of *Hermite Gaussians* centred at
:math:`P = (\alpha A+\beta B)/p`:

.. math::

   G_{ij} = \sum_{t=0}^{i+j} E_t^{ij}(\alpha,\beta,X_{AB})\,
             \Lambda_t(p, r-P),\qquad
   \Lambda_t(p,x) = \left(-\frac{\partial}{\partial P}\right)^t e^{-p(r-P)^2}.

E-Coefficients
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

The expansion coefficients :math:`E_t^{ij}` satisfy the three-term
recursion (one Cartesian direction at a time):

.. math::

   E_t^{i+1,j} &= \frac{1}{2p} E_{t-1}^{ij}
                  + X_{PA}\, E_t^{ij}
                  + (t+1)\, E_{t+1}^{ij} \\[4pt]
   E_t^{i,j+1} &= \frac{1}{2p} E_{t-1}^{ij}
                  + X_{PB}\, E_t^{ij}
                  + (t+1)\, E_{t+1}^{ij}

starting from :math:`E_0^{00} = e^{-\mu X_{AB}^2}` with
:math:`\mu = \alpha\beta/p`.

The implementation stores the full table
``E[i][j][t]`` with :math:`i,j \le 8` and :math:`t \le i+j` as a stack
array of size ``[9][9][18]`` (``ETable``).

R-Integrals
~~~~~~~~~~~~

The auxiliary Hermite integrals required for nuclear-attraction (NA)
and ERI evaluation are:

.. math::

   R_{tuv}^n = (-2p)^n\,
       \frac{\partial^t}{\partial P_x^t}
       \frac{\partial^u}{\partial P_y^u}
       \frac{\partial^v}{\partial P_z^v}
       \frac{1}{r}\bigg|_{r=|\mathbf{P}-\mathbf{C}|}

with base case

.. math::

   R_{000}^n = F_n(p\,R_{PC}^2)

and recursion [HJO2000b]_ (eq. 9.9.18):

.. math::

   R_{t+1,u,v}^n &= t\,R_{t-1,u,v}^{n+1} + X_{PC}\,R_{tuv}^{n+1} \\
   R_{t,u+1,v}^n &= u\,R_{t,u-1,v}^{n+1} + Y_{PC}\,R_{tuv}^{n+1} \\
   R_{t,u,v+1}^n &= v\,R_{t,u,v-1}^{n+1} + Z_{PC}\,R_{tuv}^{n+1}.

The table ``R[n][t][u][v]`` is stored as ``[20][20][20][20]`` doubles on the
thread-local stack.

One-Electron Integrals
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Overlap :math:`S_{\mu\nu} = \langle\mu|\nu\rangle`
****************************************************

For primitives :math:`(\mathbf{a}, \ell_a)` and :math:`(\mathbf{b}, \ell_b)`:

.. math::

   S_{\mu\nu} = E_0^{n_{x,a}\,n_{x,b}}\,E_0^{n_{y,a}\,n_{y,b}}\,E_0^{n_{z,a}\,n_{z,b}}
   \cdot \left(\frac{\pi}{p}\right)^{3/2}.

Kinetic energy :math:`T_{\mu\nu} = \langle\mu|-\tfrac{1}{2}\nabla^2|\nu\rangle`
*********************************************************************************

Using the Obara-Saika relation [OS1986]_:

.. math::

   T_{\mu\nu} = \beta(2\ell_b+3)\,S_{\mu\nu}^{(b)}
     - 2\beta^2\,S_{\mu\nu}^{(b+2)}
     - \tfrac{1}{2}\ell_b(\ell_b-1)\,S_{\mu\nu}^{(b-2)}

where :math:`S^{(b\pm 2)}` denotes the overlap integral with the
angular momentum of centre B raised/lowered by one unit (total) in the
relevant Cartesian direction, expressed via E-coefficient tables
accumulated at the same :math:`p`.

Nuclear attraction :math:`V_{\mu\nu} = \langle\mu|{-Z_A}/{r_{1A}}|\nu\rangle`
*******************************************************************************

.. math::

   V_{\mu\nu} = \frac{2\pi}{p} \sum_A (-Z_A)
       \sum_{tuv} E_t^{(x)}\,E_u^{(y)}\,E_v^{(z)}\, R_{tuv}^0

summed over all nuclear centres :math:`A`.

Two-Electron Integrals (ERIs)
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

The four-centre ERI

.. math::

   (\mu\nu|\lambda\sigma) = \iint
   \chi_\mu(\mathbf{r}_1)\chi_\nu(\mathbf{r}_1)\,\frac{1}{r_{12}}\,
   \chi_\lambda(\mathbf{r}_2)\chi_\sigma(\mathbf{r}_2)\,
   d\mathbf{r}_1\,d\mathbf{r}_2

factorises (after Gaussian product theorem applied to both pairs) as

.. math::

   (\mu\nu|\lambda\sigma)
   = \frac{2\pi^{5/2}}{p\,q\sqrt{p+q}}
     \sum_{t_1 u_1 v_1}
     \sum_{t_2 u_2 v_2}
     E_{t_1}^{(x,12)}\,E_{u_1}^{(y,12)}\,E_{v_1}^{(z,12)}\,
     E_{t_2}^{(x,34)}\,E_{u_2}^{(y,34)}\,E_{v_2}^{(z,34)}\,
     (-1)^{t_2+u_2+v_2}\,
     R_{t_1+t_2,u_1+u_2,v_1+v_2}^0

where :math:`p = \alpha_1+\alpha_2`, :math:`q = \alpha_3+\alpha_4`,
:math:`\mathbf{W} = (p\mathbf{P}+q\mathbf{Q})/(p+q)`, and the
R-integrals are evaluated at :math:`\mathbf{W}-\mathbf{P}` with
parameter :math:`\rho = pq/(p+q)`.

The Boys vector is computed once per primitive quartet with
``boys_Fvec(nmax, rho*RPQ², F)`` where :math:`n_\text{max}` is the
sum of all four angular momenta.

Shell Normalization
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

After primitive contractions are assembled, each shell is normalized so
that its diagonal overlap matrix element equals 1:

.. math::

   N_\mu = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\langle\mu|\mu\rangle}}.

This is applied to all contracted functions within the shell
simultaneously, matching the convention used by Gaussian09 and Psi4.

Direct SCF and Schwarz Screening
----------------------------------

**Direct SCF** recomputes all ERIs every iteration — no disk storage.
This scales as :math:`\mathcal{O}(N_b^4)` naively but is accelerated
by the **Schwarz inequality**: for a shell quartet :math:`(\mu\nu|\lambda\sigma)`

.. math::

   |(\mu\nu|\lambda\sigma)| \le \sqrt{(\mu\nu|\mu\nu)}\,\sqrt{(\lambda\sigma|\lambda\sigma)}.

Define the *Schwarz matrix* :math:`Q_{\mu\nu} = \sqrt{(\mu\nu|\mu\nu)}`.
Shell quartets are skipped entirely when

.. math::

   Q_{\mu\nu}^{\rm shell}\cdot Q_{\lambda\sigma}^{\rm shell} < \varepsilon_{\rm screen}

(default :math:`\varepsilon_{\rm screen} = 10^{-10}`).  Within a
surviving shell quartet, individual basis-function pairs are also
screened before accumulating into :math:`\mathbf{J}` and
:math:`\mathbf{K}`.

The J/K build exploits the 8-fold permutational symmetry of real ERIs:

.. math::

   (\mu\nu|\lambda\sigma) = (\nu\mu|\lambda\sigma) = (\mu\nu|\sigma\lambda)
   = (\lambda\sigma|\mu\nu) = \ldots

so each unique quartet is computed once.

Pulay DIIS Convergence Acceleration
--------------------------------------

Without acceleration, the SCF iteration

.. math::

   P_{\rm new} = \text{diagonalize}\bigl(F[P]\bigr)

may converge only linearly or oscillate.  **Direct Inversion in the
Iterative Subspace** (DIIS) [Pulay1980]_ constructs a better Fock matrix
as a linear combination of previous iterates:

.. math::

   \mathbf{F}_\text{DIIS} = \sum_{i=1}^m c_i\, \mathbf{F}_i

where the coefficients :math:`c_i` minimise the error norm subject to
:math:`\sum_i c_i = 1`.

Error Vector
~~~~~~~~~~~~~

The DIIS error vector is taken as the *commutator* of the Fock and
density matrices in the orthogonal AO basis:

.. math::

   \mathbf{e} = \mathbf{F}\mathbf{P}\mathbf{S} - \mathbf{S}\mathbf{P}\mathbf{F}.

When :math:`\mathbf{e} = 0` the density matrix satisfies the
idempotency and the Fock equations simultaneously, so this is a well-
motivated measure of SCF error.

DIIS Linear System
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

The DIIS equations form the bordered linear system

.. math::

   \begin{pmatrix}
   B_{11} & \cdots & B_{1m} & -1 \\
   \vdots & \ddots & \vdots & \vdots \\
   B_{m1} & \cdots & B_{mm} & -1 \\
   -1     & \cdots & -1     &  0
   \end{pmatrix}
   \begin{pmatrix} c_1 \\ \vdots \\ c_m \\ \lambda \end{pmatrix}
   =
   \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ \vdots \\ 0 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}

where :math:`B_{ij} = \langle \mathbf{e}_i | \mathbf{e}_j \rangle =
\operatorname{Tr}(\mathbf{e}_i^\top \mathbf{e}_j)`.

This is solved via ``at::linalg_solve``.  If the matrix is singular (a
degenerate subspace), the program falls back to the most recent Fock
matrix.

SCF Convergence Criterion
---------------------------

Convergence is declared when *both* of the following are satisfied
simultaneously:

.. math::

   |\Delta E| < \varepsilon \quad \text{and} \quad
   \text{RMS}(\Delta \mathbf{P}) < \varepsilon

where :math:`\varepsilon` is the user-supplied ``convergence`` threshold
(default :math:`10^{-8}`).

The initial guess for the density matrix is obtained from the
**core-Hamiltonian** (bare-nucleus) Fock matrix: diagonalise
:math:`\mathbf{H}^{\rm core}` in the orthogonal basis, occupy the
:math:`N/2` lowest orbitals, and form :math:`\mathbf{P}^{(0)}`.

References
----------

.. [MD1978]   L. E. McMurchie and E. R. Davidson, *J. Comput. Phys.* **26**,
   218 (1978).
.. [OS1986]   S. Obara and A. Saika, *J. Chem. Phys.* **84**, 3963 (1986).
.. [Pulay1980] P. Pulay, *Chem. Phys. Lett.* **73**, 393 (1980).
.. [HJO2000b]  T. Helgaker, P. Jørgensen, and J. Olsen,
   *Molecular Electronic-Structure Theory*, Wiley (2000).
